content: For ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT/OFFSET, an index on created_at alone does not satisfy the sort: SQLite must materialise a temp B-tree for the tie-break, visible as 'USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY' in EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN. The index must be on (created_at, id) — SQLite can walk a composite index backwards for an all-DESC ordering, so explicit DESC on the index columns is optional but harmless. A covering index in SQLite means every column the query touches is IN the index column list; SQLite has NO INCLUDE clause (that is Postgres/SQL Server syntax — a search result asserting CREATE INDEX ... INCLUDE for SQLite is wrong). Large OFFSET remains O(offset) even with the right index; keyset pagination on (created_at, id) is the fix at scale.
